lines.say: Cells make tissues, tissues make organs, organs make systems. No system works alone.
Nerves are fast and targeted. Hormones are slower but last longer.
Homeostasis keeps the inside steady. A sensor, a control centre and an effector.

draw.alt: Negative feedback loop returning variable to set point

lines.say: Negative feedback reverses the change. Most homeostasis works this way.
Positive feedback amplifies change, like childbirth contractions or clotting.
Heat moves by radiation, conduction, convection and evaporation.
Endotherms make heat by metabolism. Ectotherms get it from the environment.
At 30 degrees, the mouse uses 2 millilitres of oxygen per gram per hour.

draw.alt: Mouse oxygen use bar at 30 degrees

lines.say: At 10 degrees it rises to 5. It burns more fuel to stay at 37.

draw.alt: Mouse oxygen use rises as air gets colder

lines.say: Vasodilation and sweating lose heat. Vasoconstriction and shivering keep it.
Countercurrent exchange in limbs passes heat back to returning blood.
Water moves by osmosis towards higher solute concentration. Always ask: compared with what?
In the sea, drink and pee a little. Marine fish excrete salt at the gills.
In the river, drink nothing and pee a lot. Freshwater fish take up salt.

draw.alt: Water leaves marine fish and enters freshwater fish

lines.say: Ammonia for aquatic, urea for us, uric acid for the unwatered.
In the kidney, ADH increases water reabsorption when blood gets too concentrated.
Fick's law: rate depends on area times difference, divided by thickness.
Fish gills use countercurrent flow. Blood always meets water with more oxygen.

draw.alt: Water and blood flowing in opposite directions across gill

lines.say: Insects use tracheae. Air goes straight to cells, not via the blood.
Birds have air sacs that give a one way flow through the lungs.
Open circulation bathes organs in haemolymph. Closed keeps blood in vessels.
Fish have two chambers and a single circuit.
Birds and mammals have four chambers and a fully separate double circulation.
Blood goes through the heart twice: once to the lungs, once to the body.
That keeps pressure high and supports high metabolic rates.
Not every feedback loop is homeostatic. Positive feedback amplifies.
Cold blooded is misleading. A basking lizard can be warmer than a mammal.
Fish gills use countercurrent flow, not same direction flow.
Fever is a raised set point, not a failure of regulation.
